'''Charles Dwight Lahr''' (February 6, 1944 – December 26, 2016)<ref name=autogenerated2>{{cite web |title=Charles Dwight Lahr |url=https://rand-wilson.com/obituaries/obit_view.php?id=265 |access-date=25 February 2021}}</ref> was an American [[mathematician]], the first tenured [[African-American]] professor of mathematics at an Ivy League university, and a university administrator.<ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite web |title=In Memoriam: Charles Dwight Lahr |date=10 January 2017 |url=https://www.jbhe.com/2017/01/in-memoriam-charles-dwight-lahr/ |access-date=25 February 2021}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in [[Philadelphia]], Dwight Lahr attended [[Central High School (Philadelphia)|Central High School]] and graduated [[Phi Beta Kappa]] from [[Temple University]] in 1966 with a bachelor's degree in math.<ref name=autogenerated2 /> He went on to earn an M.A. in 1968 and a Ph.D. in mathematics from [[Syracuse University]] in 1972, with a dissertation entitled "Approximate identities and multipliers for certain convolution measure algebras."<ref>{{cite web |title=Alumni |url=https://thecollege.syr.edu/mathematics/graduate-studies/alumni/ |access-date=25 February 2021}}</ref> After working at [[Bell Labs]], he joined the faculty of [[Dartmouth College]] as an assistant professor in 1975. Lahr became an associate professor in 1981, served as associate dean of faculty for sciences and dean of graduate studies, and became full professor and dean of the faculty in 1984.<ref name=autogenerated3>{{cite web |title=The C. Dwight Lahr Lecture Series |url=https://math.dartmouth.edu/activities/lahr-lectures/ |access-date=25 February 2021}}</ref> In 1994, he was the founder and director of "CLIPP, a Dartmouth Summer Institute to develop computer literacy for inner city public school teachers" and to provide them computer equipment.<ref name=autogenerated3 /> He retired in 2014,<ref name=autogenerated1 /> and in 2021 Dartmouth College inaugurated the C. Dwight Lahr Lecture series.<ref name=autogenerated3 />

==Publications==
His area of specialization was [[functional analysis]], and he published 12 papers in the field. He also contributed to a textbook, ''Principles of Calculus Modeling: An Interactive Approach''.

# Lahr, Charles D. (1976). Isometric multipliers and isometric isomorphisms of 𝑙₁(𝑆). ''Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society'', 58(1), 104–108. https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-1976-0415209-7
# Jones, C. A., & Lahr, C. D. (1977). Weak and norm approximate identities are different. ''Pacific Journal of Mathematics'', 72(1), 99.
# Johnson, D. L., & Lahr, C. D. (1979a). Dual $A\sp{\ast} $-algebras of the first kind. ''Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society'', 74(2), 311. 
# Johnson, D. L., & Lahr, C. D. (1979b). Multipliers of $A\sp{\ast} $-algebras. ''Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society'', 74(2), 315. 
# Johnson, D. L., & Lahr, C. D. (1980). Multipliers of tensor products of CMA’s and Radon-Nikodým derivatives. ''Illinois Journal of Mathematics'', 24(2), 216. 
# Johnson, D. L.; Lahr, C. D. The trace class of an arbitrary Hilbert algebra. ''Comment. Math. Univ. St. Paul.'' 28 (1980), no. 1, 1--9.
